label: letter m input at position 1
explanation: Fires exactly when the second original token (t=1) is the letter m; every such step is active (no false positives). Activation is nearly constant (~0.66, max 0.756); magnitude is modulated slightly by the preceding first token (e.g. first token y gives the max, w/s/n give lower values). Does not fire on m at any other position, on other tokens at t=1, or in the delimiter/copy phases, including when m is output or fed back. The only exceptions are 19 tiny activations (~0.05 of max) on m at t=2 after the prefix d q.

issues: I could not refute the label. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.9986, F1 0.9993, mass recall 0.9999 and correlation 0.996. There are 0 false positives.

The dev-split profile matches the main claims. Activation is zero in the delimiter and copy phases. At t=1, in_tok m holds all of the activation mass (16730 of 16749 active steps). Magnitude is mean 0.658, max 0.756, so it is close to constant.

The only systematic exception is the one the explanation already states. There are 24 missed steps on the test split, and in every one I looked at, m is at t=2 after the prefix 'd q', with activation 0.05 of max. They carry 0.0% of the activation mass, so this does not affect the label in any meaningful way.
I did not check the claim that the first token changes the size (y gives the maximum; w, s and n give lower values). It is minor and does not change the verdict.
